title: onprem-airgap-offline-bundle-vendor-rke2-suse-microos-tuf-rollbacks
author: Jordan Patel
description:
Context: Customers running the Private on-prem installer on SUSE MicroOS have hit two issues in air-gapped installs: (1) TUF metadata updates may roll forward mismatched timestamps after an interrupted mirror sync, and (2) the offline bundle is missing a small set of vendor-specific runtime packages (containerd and kernel modules) that SUSE customers need for rke2. This PR updates the offline bundle generation and vendoring process to include SUSE MicroOS artifacts, hardens TUF timestamp handling for safe rollback, and exposes a rollback helper script in the installer for operators to recover a stable mirror state.

What changed (high level):
- Offline bundle: add vendor/rke2/suse-microos/ directory with containerd/CRI and pre-built kernel-module artifacts for x86_64 and aarch64 (sha256 manifests).
- Vendoring: extend vendoring pipeline to fetch SUSE MicroOS RPMs from customer-provided mirror URLs and to validate checksums with TUF metadata.
- TUF: implement conservative timestamp acceptance (only accept newer timestamp if snapshot/root are valid and timestamp "consistent" with TTL), add a rollback path that can replace timestamp.json with previous signed snapshot if a mirror sync was interrupted.
- Rollback tooling: add scripts/airgap/rollback-mirror.sh (wrapper around tuf-client commands + checksum validation) and documented usage in installer README.
- Helm chart: bump private-installer chart version and add optional values.suseMicroOS.enable to toggle inclusion of SUSE artifacts in offline bundles.
- Tests: integration test for offline bundle generation that validates presence of suse artifacts and TUF rollback scenario simulated with a bad timestamp.

Reasoning: By vendoring the minimal SUSE runtime artifacts we avoid forcing customers to perform complex manual mirroring steps. Conservative TUF timestamp handling prevents accidental acceptance of partially-synced repositories and provides an operator path to safely roll back to a previously known-good timestamp.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add SUSE MicroOS artifacts to bundle generator
- [x] Extend vendoring CI to pull from configured SUSE mirrors (mocked in CI)
- [x] Implement TUF timestamp acceptance policy + rollback helper
- [x] Add Helm values docs and example config for SUSE vendors
- [x] Add integration tests and unit tests for new utils
- [x] Run full airgap e2e on rke2 (local infra)

Notes: This is additive and behind a feature flag (values.suseMicroOS.enable=false by default). No changes to default bundles unless the flag is enabled. The vendoring pipeline requires credentials to the SUSE mirror and will continue to support customers providing their own mirror tarball instead.

release_notes:
- Added optional SUSE MicroOS artifact vendoring for on-prem air-gapped offline bundles (values.suseMicroOS.enable = true).
- Hardened TUF timestamp acceptance policy to avoid partial mirror acceptance; added rollback helper script (installer/airgap/rollback-mirror.sh).
- Installer now verifies bundle checksums on unpack to detect corruption.
(Operators: enable the feature explicitly; see docs/onprem/airgap-suse.md for migration steps)
security_impact: low: added vendored runtime artifacts and additional signature/checksum checks. No new network calls by default; mirror fetch still requires operator-provided credentials.
backout_plan: Revert chart bump and remove suse artifacts from bundle generator. Installer continues to accept previous bundles. For broken mirror sync, operators can run rollback-mirror.sh to restore previous timestamp.json and re-run mirror sync.
notes_for_release_manager: This change is behind a feature flag; coordinate release notes with marketing. Recommend staging rollout to a few Dedicated customers and inform SRE on metrics (installer.tuf.timestamp_rejected).
